schedule.notes: Drop-in; sensory-friendly session with relaxed expectations

activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Raleigh Free Museum Sensory Morning
activities.description: Hands-on exhibits glow and hum at a gentler pace while young explorers touch, build, and discover. Smiles and curious questions fill every gallery.
accessibility_notes: Elevator access to every gallery and ramps at entrances
Reduced lighting and sound with a calm-down room
Seating and rest spots throughout the exhibits
activities.best_time: First Sunday mornings, 9-11am, before regular crowds arrive.
activities.caregiver_tip: Pack headphones or a favorite comfort item just in case.

schedule.notes: Free community morning on the first Sunday of each month

activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Raleigh Adaptive Climbing Night
activities.price_note: About $15-20 per session; scholarships may be available
activities.description: Teens and young adults clip in, reach high, and cheer each other up the wall with adaptive gear and friendly coaches. Every summit is a victory party.
accessibility_notes: Step-free access to the climbing gym and accessible restrooms
Adaptive harnesses and wall routes with trained staff
Seated belay and spotting options available
activities.best_time: Thursday evenings, 6-8pm, with a social vibe.
activities.caregiver_tip: Wear comfortable clothes and ask staff about gear fitting at check-in.
activities.venue: Indoor climbing gym adaptive program space

schedule.notes: Weekly evening session; sign up in advance

activities.how_to_join: Register with the gym's adaptive program staff before your first visit.

activities.name: Fells Point Roll & Stroll Path
activities.description: A smooth, shaded loop invites rolling, strolling, and spotting birds and butterflies along the way. Families linger at every bench to soak in the fresh air.
accessibility_notes: Firm paved surface with gentle slopes
Benches with companion space along the route
Accessible restrooms near the trailhead
activities.best_time: Mornings, 8-11am, when the path is cool and calm.
activities.caregiver_tip: Bring water and a hat, and plan a rest stop at the halfway bench.
activities.venue: Park loop trail near the main entrance

schedule.notes: Open daily; drop-in, quietest in the morning

activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Hampden Inclusive Playground
activities.description: Ramps, sensory panels, and roomy swings let every child climb, spin, and shout with joy. Laughter echoes across the soft, springy surface.
accessibility_notes: Poured rubber surfacing that rolls easily
Ramped play structures with transfer stations
Shaded seating and accessible restrooms nearby
activities.best_time: Weekday mornings, 9-11am, before the afternoon rush.
activities.caregiver_tip: Visit early on warm days since shade fills up fast.

schedule.notes: Open daily; drop-in play

activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Baltimore Inclusive Dance & Movement Class
activities.description: Music fills the studio as dancers of every ability swirl, sway, and roll in joyful rhythm. Instructors celebrate every unique way of moving.
accessibility_notes: Step-free studio with open floor space for wheelchairs
Visual cues and signed directions for hearing differences
Chairs available for seated and standing dancers
activities.best_time: Tuesday evenings, 5:30-6:30pm.
activities.caregiver_tip: Wear comfy clothes and bring a favorite song idea to share.

schedule.notes: Weekly drop-in class

activities.how_to_join: Sign up with the arts center front desk or just drop in.

activities.caregiver_tip: Start near Children's Fairyland so little ones have a fun goal at the end.

schedule.notes: Public path, open every day; weekend afternoons get busy

activities.how_to_join: Just show up and pick a starting point by the lake.
activities.name: Lake Merritt Loop Roll & Stroll
activities.description: A flat, paved loop around Oakland's lake with ducks, pelicans and skyline views. Roll a short stretch or the whole loop, about three miles, and turn back whenever you like.
accessibility_notes: Mostly flat paved path around the lake
Benches all along the way for rest stops
Nearby downtown sidewalks and transit; check parking near your starting point
activities.best_time: Open daily; mornings are calmer

activities.caregiver_tip: Bring warm layers and gloves; the rink is cold even when the bench is cheering.
activities.how_to_join: Contact BORP to ask about the current season and a try-it session.
activities.name: BORP Youth Sled Hockey (with Oakland Ice Center)
activities.price_note: Low cost; confirm current fees with BORP
activities.description: Northern California's ongoing youth sled hockey program: kids fly across the ice in custom sleds, stick-handling and scoring with a real team. Sleds and equipment are provided.
accessibility_notes: Custom sleds and equipment provided by the program
Coaches experienced with wheelchair users
Ask about group transportation, which BORP has offered youth participants
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Email or call BORP to book a ride or ask about youth group rides.
activities.name: BORP Adaptive Cycling Center
activities.price_note: Membership or program enrollment may be required; confirm fees
activities.description: A fleet of more than 65 adaptive cycles, including youth sizes: handcycles, trikes and tandems. Group youth rides are escorted by trained volunteers.
accessibility_notes: Adaptive bikes in youth and adult sizes
Trained volunteers on group youth rides
Hours are seasonal; book ahead
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Contact BORP's youth sports team to ask about practices and sign-up.
activities.name: BORP Youth Wheelchair Basketball & Power Soccer
activities.price_note: Low cost; confirm current fees with BORP
activities.description: Team practices where kids who use manual or power chairs learn the game, make friends and compete. Power soccer is built for power-chair users.
accessibility_notes: Sports chairs and equipment through the program
Power soccer designed for power-chair users
Also ask about Jr. Adventures, BORP's non-competitive outings
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Buy admission at the gate or on their website.
activities.name: Children's Fairyland
activities.description: A storybook park on the shore of Lake Merritt with puppet shows, small rides and fairy-tale sets made for young children. A beloved Oakland classic.
accessibility_notes: Ask staff for the most accessible route through the park
Lakeside location next to the flat Lake Merritt path
Call ahead about accessible restrooms and changing space
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets on their website or at the gate.
activities.name: Oakland Zoo
activities.description: Lions, giraffes and a gondola ride up to the California Trail with views over the bay. Some paths are hilly, so plan your route.
accessibility_notes: Ask about the gondola to the California Trail and wheelchair loading
Some paths are steep; ask for an accessibility map
Check their website for accessibility services and sensory resources
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets on their website.
activities.name: Chabot Space & Science Center
activities.description: Planetarium shows, hands-on space exhibits and big telescopes up in the Oakland hills. A cozy indoor adventure for curious kids.
accessibility_notes: Ask about accessible parking and elevator access
Planetarium shows can be loud and dark; ask about seating near exits
Check their site for sensory-friendly events
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.how_to_join: Find a storytime on the library's events calendar.
activities.name: Oakland Public Library Storytimes
activities.description: Songs, stories and wiggles for little ones at Oakland's library branches. A free, easy outing on a rainy day.
accessibility_notes: Ask your branch about accessible entrances and seating
Libraries can often help with large print and audiobooks
Check the branch calendar for sensory-friendly storytimes
activities.best_time: Check your branch's storytime calendar

activities.neighborhood: Peninsula & South Bay (a drive from Oakland)
activities.how_to_join: Free and open to the public; see their site for locations.
activities.name: Magical Bridge Playgrounds (Peninsula & South Bay)
activities.description: Playgrounds designed from the ground up for kids of every ability, with wheelchair-friendly surfacing and sensory play. Worth the drive from Oakland for a big day out.
accessibility_notes: Designed for people of all abilities
Smooth surfacing for wheelchairs and walkers
Several locations; check which is closest
activities.best_time: Check today's hours and prices on their website before you go

activities.caregiver_tip: Spanish-speaking tour guides lead several tours each week.
activities.how_to_join: Just walk in; admission is free.
activities.name: Yale Peabody Museum
activities.description: Dinosaurs, including the famous Brontosaurus in the Great Hall, in a museum reopened after a big renovation. Free for everyone, every visit.
accessibility_notes: Step-free entrances with ramps and large elevators inside
Accessible parking at Whitney Avenue & Humphrey Street (lot 22v)
Sighted guides available on request in advance by email
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go

activities.venue: Yale University Art Gallery, Chapel Street
activities.how_to_join: Free; just walk in.
activities.name: Yale University Art Gallery
activities.description: One of the country's oldest university art museums, with everything from ancient art to modern masterpieces. A calm, free indoor outing.
accessibility_notes: See the gallery's accessibility page for entrances and elevators
Quiet galleries with room to roll
Ask at the desk about seating and rest spots
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go

activities.venue: Yale Center for British Art, Chapel Street
activities.how_to_join: Free; just walk in.
activities.name: Yale Center for British Art
activities.description: Light-filled galleries of paintings, prints and sculpture in a landmark building. Free, peaceful and easy to explore in a short visit.
accessibility_notes: Check their visit page for accessible entrances and elevators
Galleries are spacious and calm
Ask about family activity guides
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go

activities.venue: New Haven Free Public Library branches
activities.how_to_join: Find a storytime on the library's events calendar.
activities.name: New Haven Free Public Library Storytimes
activities.description: Songs, books and wiggles for little ones at New Haven's library branches. A free, cozy outing on a cold day.
accessibility_notes: Ask your branch about accessible entrances and seating
Libraries can help with large print and audiobooks
Check the calendar for sensory-friendly events
activities.best_time: Check your branch's storytime calendar

schedule.notes: Public green, open every day

activities.how_to_join: Just show up.
activities.name: New Haven Green Roll & Stroll
activities.description: The historic town green at the heart of downtown, with flat paths, big trees and people-watching. Pair it with a free museum a few blocks away.
accessibility_notes: Flat paths across the green
Benches around the edges
Watch for snow and ice on curb cuts in winter
activities.best_time: Open daily; sunny afternoons are lovely

activities.caregiver_tip: Younger than 16? Ask Gaylord and CPAC about youth options nearby.
activities.how_to_join: Contact the Gaylord Sports Association to ask about joining or a try-it day.
activities.name: Gaylord Sports Association: Wolfpack Sled Hockey & adaptive sports (ages 16+)
activities.price_note: Fees vary by program; confirm with Gaylord
activities.description: Connecticut's largest adaptive sports program, with 17 sports, including the Gaylord Wolfpack, the state's only sled hockey team. Programs are for ages 16 and up.
accessibility_notes: For people 16+ with a physical disability or visual impairment
Adaptive equipment through the program
Recreational and competitive options year-round
activities.best_time: Sled hockey season runs roughly September to May; check their calendar

activities.name: Spaulding Sledgehogs Youth Sled Hockey
activities.price_note: Fees apply to some sled hockey sessions; check current prices with Spaulding
activities.description: Spaulding Adaptive Sports Centers' Sledgehogs is greater Boston's youth sled hockey team, with youth-only practices plus clinics and games around the region and beyond. Kids of all abilities glide, pass and score from the seat of a sled, and teammates quickly become a second family.
accessibility_notes: Coaching and sleds/equipment are provided in Spaulding sled hockey sessions
Offers both recreational and competitive levels of play
Ask which rink this season's practices use and about accessible locker rooms and parking
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Pack extra layers, a blanket and warm gloves for both the player and the bench crew; rinks are chilly.
activities.venue: Greater Boston ice rinks (Spaulding Adaptive Sports Centers program)
activities.how_to_join: Pre-register for practices on the Spaulding Adaptive Sports Centers sled hockey page, or email spauldingsledhockey@partners.org to ask about a first try.

activities.name: Miracle League of Massachusetts Baseball
activities.price_note: Free to players; the league says it is provided at no cost to families
activities.description: Every player gets to bat, run the bases and hear the crowd cheer on the Joseph Lalli Miracle Field, a specially built field at NARA Park. Volunteer buddies help where needed, so the whole afternoon is about joy, not keeping score.
accessibility_notes: The Miracle Field has a flat, rubberized surface so players using wheelchairs and walkers can move around the bases
Youth league for players about ages 5 to 21, plus a separate adult league
Ask about accessible parking and restrooms at NARA Park when you register
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Bring sunscreen, water and a folding chair for the sidelines, and let the volunteer buddies take a turn while you cheer.
activities.venue: Joseph Lalli Miracle Field, NARA Park
activities.how_to_join: Register through the Youth registration form on the league's website before the season starts.

activities.name: DCR Adaptive Ice Skating at Porrazzo Memorial Rink
activities.price_note: Free: entry and equipment are free of charge (DCR Universal Access Program)
activities.description: The state's Universal Access Program turns a public rink into a place where everyone gets on the ice, whether in their own wheelchair, an ice sled or a skate walker. Families, friends and support staff are welcome to skate alongside.
accessibility_notes: Skaters can use a wheelchair, an ice sled, a skate walker, ice grippers or regular skates on the ice
Adaptive equipment is provided free
Pre-registration is required; ask about age guidelines for younger children when you sign up
activities.best_time: Winter 2026-27 Wednesday sessions listed by DCR, e.g. Dec. 9, 2026, 11 a.m.-1:30 p.m.; further dates listed for Jan. 6, Feb. 3 and Mar. 3, 2027. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Bring a winter coat, hat and gloves; the rink is cold even for people watching from the boards.
activities.how_to_join: Pre-register with the DCR Universal Access Program (DCR.UniversalAccess@mass.gov); groups submit a registration sheet and release forms a week ahead.

activities.name: Martin's Park
activities.description: Built in memory of Martin Richard, this waterfront playground in the Seaport was designed so children of every ability can climb, explore and play together, including on its big play ship. Sloping paths, gardens and water play make it a favorite stop next to Boston Children's Museum.
accessibility_notes: Sloping paths and hills let children with mobility disabilities reach the top of the play areas
Signs point out the inclusive routes and play elements
Quieter, plant-filled corners offer a break for kids who get overstimulated; the park has no dedicated parking lot, so plan on a nearby garage
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Pair it with a Boston Children's Museum visit next door so you can trade between indoor and outdoor play.
activities.venue: Martin's Park at Children's Wharf Park, 64 Sleeper Street
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Gronk Playground on the Esplanade
activities.description: Opened in 2025 on the old Charlesbank Playground site, this riverside playground was built to be fully ADA-accessible, with mini duck boats, small Boston landmarks and a 40-yard dash. It sits right next to the Alfond Spray Deck and Teddy Ebersol's Red Sox Fields, so there is plenty to do in one stop.
accessibility_notes: Described by the Esplanade Association and DCR as a fully ADA-accessible playground
Design plans included rubberized surfacing and a ground-level merry-go-round for wheelchair access
Accessible portable restrooms are next to Teddy Ebersol's Red Sox Fields and the Alfond Spray Deck (seasonal); ask the Esplanade Association about current restroom hours
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Use the four accessible parking spaces at the Blossom Street entrance, or take the T to Science Park/West End.
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Charles River Esplanade Paths
activities.description: Three miles of riverside park with more than five miles of paved paths, sailboats on the Charles and skyline views at every turn. Roll as far as you like, then rest at a playground, the Hatch Shell or the water's edge.
accessibility_notes: Over five miles of paved paths; width and smoothness vary, but the Esplanade Association calls them largely welcoming to all visitors
The Frances Appleton Pedestrian Bridge at Charles Circle is the most accessible way in; there are also at-grade entrances at each end of the park
Four accessible parking spaces at the Blossom Street entrance; Charles/MGH is the nearby T station with an ADA footbridge
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Restrooms are typically open dawn to dusk from mid-April to mid-October, so plan longer outings for the warmer months.
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Story Times at the Boston Public Library Children's Library
activities.price_note: Free; the library says all of its programs are free and open to the public
activities.description: The Children's Library at the Central Library in Copley Square hosts story times for little ones (recent listings include ages 0-5 and 0-7), full of songs, rhymes and picture books. It is a cozy, welcoming way to spend a morning or afternoon together.
accessibility_notes: The 700 Boylston Street entrance is at sidewalk level, and the Glass and West elevators reach the second-floor Children's Library
Request ASL or other interpretation in advance through the contact on the event listing
Magnifiers and an adaptive computer station are available, and staff can help with a Perkins Library application for Braille and accessible materials
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Ask for accommodations well before the event; the library recommends contacting the Children's Room ahead of time.
activities.venue: Boston Public Library, Central Library in Copley Square (Children's Library)
activities.how_to_join: Check the BPL events calendar for current story times; most are drop-in.

activities.name: Boston Children's Museum: Morningstar Access
activities.price_note: General admission is listed at $24 for ages 1 and up (under 12 months free); check Morningstar Access pricing when you pre-register
activities.description: Morningstar Access opens the museum at quieter times for children with special or medical needs and their families, with a cap of 100 guests. Kids can climb, splash and pretend at their own pace without the usual crowds.
accessibility_notes: Building and exhibits are wheelchair accessible, and the main elevator serves all three floors
Free child and adult manual wheelchairs to borrow, plus sound-reducing earmuffs and assistive listening devices at the Admissions Desk
Wheelchair-accessible family restrooms on every floor and a height-adjustable adult changing table in the first aid room (staff unlock it on request)
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Grab the museum's pre-visit Social Story to help your child know what to expect, then head next door to Martin's Park afterward.
activities.how_to_join: Pre-register for a monthly Morningstar Access date on the museum's website; registration is required.

activities.name: Museum of Science, Boston
activities.price_note: Listed at $33 adults and $28 ages 3-11 (under 3 free); personal care assistants accompanying a visitor with a disability get in free. Check current prices on their website
activities.description: From live science shows to the Planetarium, the Museum of Science is a big, hands-on adventure for curious kids of every age. Its Access Hours and quieter weekend mornings make it easier to explore at your own pace.
accessibility_notes: Free loans of manual, pediatric and bariatric wheelchairs, strollers and scooters at the Information Desk
Audio description for pre-recorded Omni and 4-D Theater shows and free Aira sighted-guide service
ASL interpretation for live shows (in-person interpreters with two weeks' notice); Access Hours every other month and Soft Light, Soft Sound Planetarium shows
activities.best_time: Weekend mornings 9-11 a.m. or weekday afternoons after 2 p.m. during the school year are usually quieter
activities.caregiver_tip: Email the Accessibility Coordinator before your visit to plan seating for shows and ask about the next Access Hours.
activities.how_to_join: Buy timed tickets online; contact the accessibility team in advance for interpreters.

activities.name: New England Aquarium
activities.price_note: Free for visitors using their own wheelchairs and for visitors with visual impairments; other family members pay regular admission (listed at $39.95 adults, $30.95 ages 3-11, 2 and under free). Check current prices on their website
activities.description: Ocean animals of every shape and size wait on Boston's waterfront, and kids who use their own wheelchairs get in free. The Aquarium is KultureCity certified, so staff are trained to welcome visitors with sensory needs.
accessibility_notes: Free wheelchair loans for ticketed guests (ID required) and elevators in the Tropical Gallery and West Wing
Sensory kits with noise-canceling headphones, fidget tools and picture-communication cards, plus quiet spaces in the lower West Wing and first-aid room
Description panels throughout for visitors who are deaf or hard of hearing; assistive listening and captioning devices in the Simons Theatre
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Sign up on the accessibility page for alerts about the Aquarium's Sensory Events with smaller crowds and lower noise.
activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets online or at the door; ask at the Information Desk for wheelchairs or sensory kits.

activities.name: Courage Kenny Adaptive Sports & Recreation: youth wheelchair basketball, power soccer and more
activities.price_note: Fees vary by program; Courage Kenny says financial barriers won't prevent participation and offers a cost share/scholarship application on request
activities.description: Courage Kenny's youth wheelchair basketball program has developmental, prep and junior varsity teams, and its Jr. Rolling Timberwolves have won three national championships. Power soccer (played from power wheelchairs), wheelchair lacrosse and more round out a program that welcomes kids as young as five.
accessibility_notes: Wheelchair basketball, power soccer and wheelchair lacrosse are held at the Courage Kenny gym in Golden Valley
Teams are split by level, from developmental to junior varsity, so beginners have a place to start
Ask whether loaner sport wheelchairs are available for new players and which team fits your child's age
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Ask for the cost share/scholarship application when you first call so money never decides whether your child plays.
activities.how_to_join: Sign the participation forms and waivers, then register through CK Active online or contact Courage Kenny Sports & Recreation to ask which youth team or try-it option fits.

activities.name: Minneapolis Parks Therapeutic Recreation & Inclusion support
activities.price_note: Program fees vary by activity; a personal assistant doesn't pay drop-in entry fees. Check current prices on their website
activities.description: Every Minneapolis Park & Recreation Board program is open to people with and without disabilities, and the Inclusion Team builds individualized support so your child can join the fun. Supports can include picture schedules, sensory-friendly spaces, sign language interpretation and 1:1 staff support.
accessibility_notes: Accommodations are individualized and follow the ADA, including sign language interpretation and 1:1 staff support
For drop-in open gym and pools, a personal assistant can come along and checks in at the front desk
Ask which recreation center near you has the program and space your child needs
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Request inclusion support at least two weeks before the program starts so staff can plan with you.
activities.venue: Minneapolis Park & Recreation Board recreation centers (citywide)
activities.how_to_join: Register for any MPRB program and choose the inclusion support option online, tell registration staff, or email the Inclusion Team at inclusion@minneapolisparks.org.

activities.name: Lake Harriet paved lake loop (Chain of Lakes)
activities.price_note: Free to visit; a pay parking lot is available
activities.description: Roll around one of Minneapolis' favorite lakes on a paved walking path of about 2.75 miles, with a separate bike path alongside. Summer brings free concerts and movies at the Lake Harriet Band Shell.
accessibility_notes: Paved walking trail of about 2.75 miles, with a separate paved bike trail
Pay parking lot on site
Restrooms at regional park facilities close for the off-season, so plan ahead in colder months
activities.best_time: Park open daily, 6 am to midnight in developed areas. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: The loop is long, so pick a turnaround point before you start and enjoy the lake views both ways.
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Wabun Universal Access Play Area at Minnehaha Regional Park
activities.price_note: Free; the park has both pay and free parking lots
activities.description: Minneapolis' first universally accessible play area sits near Minnehaha Falls, with cabins, tents and a play car and camper inspired by the park's history. Rubber surfacing and ramps up onto the structure let kids who roll and kids who run play side by side.
accessibility_notes: Rubberized surfacing throughout the play area
Multiple ramps lead up onto the play structure, plus a quiet area
Ask the park board about current parking and path conditions, since construction has affected access nearby
activities.best_time: Park open daily, 6 am to midnight in developed areas. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Reserve one of the Wabun picnic shelters if you're bringing a big group of family and friends.
activities.venue: Wabun Picnic Area, Minnehaha Regional Park
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; picnic shelters can be reserved through the park board.

activities.name: Como Park Zoo & Conservatory
activities.price_note: Free admission; a voluntary donation ($8 adults, $5 children) is appreciated but not required. Wheelchair rental is $10/day
activities.description: Say hello to animals and wander a glass conservatory full of plants, all with free admission in St. Paul. Sensory Friendly Early Entry mornings give families a calmer hour before the gates open to everyone.
accessibility_notes: Wheelchairs ($10/day) and electric scooters ($30/day) can be rented on site; they can't be reserved ahead
A social narrative, visual schedule and sensory map are available on the website
Sensory Friendly Early Entry runs 9 to 10 AM on listed dates
activities.best_time: Zoo open daily 10 AM to 4 PM; Conservatory open 10 AM to 4 PM Tuesday to Sunday through April 30, 2027. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Download the sensory map and visual schedule before you go so your child knows what's coming.
activities.how_to_join: No tickets needed; just arrive during open hours.

activities.name: Minnesota Children's Museum
activities.price_note: Online advance tickets $17.95 to $19.95, walk-up $24.95, income-based All Play tickets $5; personal care attendants are free with the person they assist
activities.description: Climb, splash, build and pretend in a museum where every exhibit is designed to be wheelchair accessible. Quiet comfort rooms and low-stimulation spaces help kids reset whenever they need a break.
accessibility_notes: Every exhibit is designed to be wheelchair accessible
Comfort rooms on the first floor (near Shipwreck Adventures) and second floor (in Sprouts)
Visual timers, noise-reducing headphones and universal cuffs can be checked out at the box office
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Park in the World Trade Center ramp and take the skyway in, and ask about All Play pricing if you have an EBT or WIC card.
activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets online in advance for the best price, or at the door.

activities.name: Minneapolis Institute of Art (Mia)
activities.price_note: General admission is always free; some special exhibitions and events are ticketed
activities.description: Explore art from around the world for free, with no tickets or reservations needed for the permanent collection. Let your child choose a favorite gallery and make it a family tradition.
accessibility_notes: Wheelchair-accessible entrances and galleries
Wheelchairs are available first come, first served; ask Visitor Experience about reserving one ahead
The free Bloomberg Connects app offers audio content and language support
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Because it's free, short visits are perfect: see a few galleries, then head home happy.
activities.how_to_join: Walk in during open hours; no tickets needed for general admission.

activities.name: Children's Theatre Company accessible performances (sensory friendly, ASL and audio described)
activities.price_note: Ticket prices vary by show and seat; check current prices on their website
activities.description: Each season, Children's Theatre Company sets aside sensory-friendly, ASL-interpreted and audio-described performances so the whole family can enjoy live theatre together. Sensory-friendly shows keep the house lights low and sound gentler, developed with Fraser and the Autism Society of Minnesota.
accessibility_notes: Step-free wheelchair rows in both theatres (Row O on the UnitedHealth Group Stage, Row A on the Cargill Stage) and accessible restrooms
Free assistive listening headsets, ASL-interpreted and audio-described performances
Large print programs and Sensory Tours on request through the Ticket Office
activities.best_time: Published accessible performances, e.g. How the Grinch Stole Christmas! sensory friendly Nov 29, 2026 at 5pm and Jan 2, 2027 at 11am, ASL/AD Dec 5, 2026 at 11am. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Request wheelchair seating when you book, and read the social story together before the show.
activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets online or through the Ticket Office and ask for any accommodations when you book.

activities.name: Three Rivers Park District adapted equipment (all-terrain wheelchairs, sit-skis, beach wheelchairs)
activities.price_note: The adapted equipment page lists no fee for most items (fees are shown only for things like child trailers); confirm when you reserve
activities.description: Three Rivers Park District lends adapted gear so families can explore its parks together, from all-terrain wheelchairs on nature trails to sit-skis in winter. Handcycles and supported kayaks are available through scheduled Outdoor Recreation School programs.
accessibility_notes: Manual all-terrain wheelchairs, including child sizes at Eastman and Richardson Nature Centers
Beach wheelchairs and ADA ramps into the water at Elm Creek and Lake Minnetonka swim ponds; sit-skis at several ski chalets
Assistive listening devices at several nature centers; ask which equipment is at the park you plan to visit
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Call the specific park ahead to hold the right-size chair; early inquiry is encouraged.
activities.venue: Three Rivers Park District parks (e.g., Elm Creek Park Reserve, Eastman and Richardson Nature Centers)
activities.neighborhood: Western and southern Twin Cities suburbs (e.g., Maple Grove)
activities.how_to_join: Contact the park you plan to visit, or the Outdoor Recreation School for equipment used in scheduled programs.

activities.name: MacPhail Center for Music: adaptive lessons and music therapy
activities.price_note: Tuition is individualized; need-based sliding-scale financial aid is available, and MacPhail can bill Fiscal Management Services for CDCS funds. Check current prices on their website
activities.description: Adaptive lessons let kids who learn music differently, including those with physical disabilities, play and sing with a board-certified music therapist who tailors every lesson. No musical experience is needed, just curiosity and joy.
accessibility_notes: Lessons are designed for students with physical, cognitive or emotional challenges
Individual sessions in person or online through MacPhail Live Online
Ask about step-free access and room setup at the location you choose
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: If your child has CDCS waiver funds, ask whether MacPhail can bill your Fiscal Management Services provider directly.
activities.venue: MacPhail Center for Music (Minneapolis, plus Apple Valley, Chanhassen and online)
activities.how_to_join: Complete the online music therapy intake form or call to schedule a short intake interview; placement with a therapist usually follows within a few days.

activities.name: Outdoors for All Adaptive Cycling at Magnuson Park
activities.price_note: On-site daily adaptive bike rentals at Magnuson Park are free during the season; taking a bike off-site or overnight carries standard rental fees
activities.description: Outdoors for All runs one of the country's biggest adaptive bike fleets, with hand- and foot-powered trikes so kids can feel the wind off Lake Washington on wheels that fit their body. During the season the Magnuson Park center lends bikes free for on-site rides, and its sister center at Lake Sammamish State Park in Issaquah is free for riders with disabilities ages 7 and up.
accessibility_notes: Hand- and foot-powered trikes are available for children ages 7 and up
Every rider must wear a helmet; bikes are first-come, first-served
Ask whether staff can help with transfers; at the Lake Sammamish center's free TrackChair, staff can't assist with transfers, so bring a support person
activities.best_time: Seasonal: in 2026 the Magnuson center ran May 1 to October 18, 7 days a week, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with some holiday and Sunday closures. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Arrive early on sunny weekends since bikes are first-come, first-served, and pack a helmet that fits your rider.
activities.venue: Magnuson Park Adaptive Cycling Center (Outdoors for All), 6344 NE 74th St
activities.how_to_join: Drop in during the season for an on-site rental, or email acc-magnuson@outdoorsforall.org with questions; register on their site for camps and Learn to Ride a Bike sessions.

activities.name: Seattle Adaptive Sports Youth Wheelchair Basketball, Sled Hockey and Power Soccer
activities.price_note: Fees aren't published online; ask Seattle Adaptive Sports about current costs
activities.description: Seattle Adaptive Sports, a Paralympic Sport Club, fields coed youth wheelchair basketball teams from the Micro Sonics (ages 4-7) up through Prep and Varsity, plus a new youth sled hockey team for ages 8-18. Power soccer has no age limit, so the whole crew can find a court where they shine.
accessibility_notes: Wheelchair basketball chairs are provided, and regular wheelchair use isn't required to play
Sled hockey needs no prior hockey experience or equipment; ask whether sleds are provided
Power soccer players need to operate the equipment independently; ask about chair availability
activities.best_time: Power soccer: Saturdays 10 a.m. to noon at Meadowbrook Community Center; wheelchair basketball practices weekly during the school year (ask for location). Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Email ahead to set up a visit to a training session so your athlete can meet the coaches and teammates first.
activities.venue: Various Seattle gyms and rinks; power soccer meets at Meadowbrook Community Center
activities.how_to_join: Email info@seattleadaptivesports.org and ask to attend a training session to try a sport.

activities.name: Seattle Parks and Recreation Specialized Programs
activities.price_note: Fees vary by program; scholarships may be available with proof of income, and the program says it accepts DDA (DDCS) respite funds where applicable. Check current prices on their website
activities.description: The City of Seattle's own recreation team for people with disabilities runs summer day camps for ages 4-21, overnight camp for ages 6-21, youth weekend programs and trips, and teen and young adult afterschool programs. It's a wonderful way for kids to make friends, try new things and give caregivers a little breathing room.
accessibility_notes: Run by Seattle Parks' dedicated Specialized Programs unit for people with disabilities
Ask about staff-to-participant ratios and help with transfers, feeding or personal care
Ask whether outings and trips use wheelchair-accessible transportation
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Seasonal registration opens early (fall 2026 registration began September 1), so mark the brochure release on your calendar.
activities.venue: Specialized Programs office, Magnuson Park Building 30, 6310 NE 74th St
activities.neighborhood: Magnuson Park / Sand Point, Seattle (programs run citywide)
activities.how_to_join: Call (206) 684-4950 or email PKS_Specialized_Programs@seattle.gov; camp registration uses the Camp Registration and Participant Information forms on their page.

activities.name: Seattle Children's PlayGarden Free Play
activities.price_note: Free and open to the public; no registration for Free Play
activities.description: This one-acre, fully fenced garden and playground was built so kids with disabilities can play side by side with siblings and friends, with friendly staff on site during open play. A 2026 renovation swapped wood chips for turf, so wheels, walkers and bare feet can roam everywhere.
accessibility_notes: Artificial turf replaced wood chips, making it wheelchair and stroller friendly
Play structures are low and wide, so it's easy to lift a child from a wheelchair onto a ride; the seesaw and spinning ring work for kids in chairs
Ask about accessible restrooms and parking when you visit
activities.best_time: Outside summer camp season the PlayGarden is open daily, sunrise to sunset (summer hours differ). Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: In summer, ask about the free Saturday wheelchair basketball the PlayGarden has hosted with Seattle Adaptive Sports and Rainier Adaptive Sports.
activities.venue: Seattle Children's PlayGarden (Seattle PlayGarden), 1745 24th Ave S at Colman Playground
activities.how_to_join: Just come play; call (206) 325-5576 about camps (ages 3.5-21), preschool and young adult programs.

activities.name: Inspiration Playground at Bellevue Downtown Park
activities.description: Bellevue built this universally accessible playground with the Bellevue Rotary Club so kids of every ability can play and explore at their own pace. Its features engage sight, sound, scent and touch, and in summer the water spray adds a splash of joy.
accessibility_notes: The City of Bellevue describes it as a universally accessible play experience with features that engage the senses
A reviewer notes multiple inclusive swing options and a braille map at the entrance
Restrooms are next to the playground; a reviewer noted some parking curb cuts don't line up with access aisles, so scout your path
activities.best_time: Open year-round; water spray typically runs from the Friday of Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Bring a towel and a change of clothes in summer; the water spray is hard to resist.
activities.how_to_join: Drop in; no registration needed.

activities.name: Green Lake Park Inner Loop
activities.description: Green Lake's 2.8-mile paved inner loop is one of Seattle's favorite car-free paths, with lake views, ducks and plenty of company. Roll a lap, stop for a picnic, or simply turn back whenever your crew is ready.
accessibility_notes: The 2.8-mile inner loop is paved
Wheeled users have the outside lane (one way, follow the arrows, 10 mph limit); motorized wheelchairs are the only motorized devices allowed
Restrooms are listed among park amenities; ask Seattle Parks which ones are accessible
activities.best_time: Park open daily, 4 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: On busy weekends, follow the lane arrows and pull aside at a wide spot when you need a break.
activities.venue: Green Lake Park, 7201 E Green Lake Dr N
activities.how_to_join: Just show up; no registration needed.

activities.name: Woodland Park Zoo
activities.price_note: Check current prices on their website; interpreters and one-to-one aides get free admission (except ticketed events like ZooTunes)
activities.description: Seattle's zoo has published an Accessibility Guide with a trail-conditions map and a Sensory Map pointing to quiet spots to relax and lively spots to romp. Blind and low-vision guests can even request a trained volunteer sighted guide for a day of animal wonder.
accessibility_notes: Manual wheelchairs and electric scooters can be rented at Guest Services (first come, first served); EBT/Washington Quest, WIC and foster and kinship families get 50% off manual wheelchair rentals
Request a sighted guide with 14 days' notice, or a certified sign language interpreter through the zoo's request form
An adult-sized changing table is in the family restroom near the West Guest Entry/ZooStore; accessible stalls are marked on the Accessibility Map
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Download the Accessibility Guide before your visit to plan the smoothest paths around the hills.
activities.how_to_join: Buy tickets online and use the zoo's access page to request a sighted guide or interpreter.

activities.name: Pacific Science Center Sensory-Friendly Hours
activities.price_note: ParentMap reports admission to Sensory-Friendly Hours is free; confirm when you reserve tickets
activities.description: About once a month, Pacific Science Center opens early or stays late with softer lighting, lower noise and hands-on exhibits adjusted for a calmer visit. It's a relaxed way for curious kids to explore science without the crowds.
accessibility_notes: Free wheelchairs at the Main Entry Information Desk (ID required as a deposit); restrooms are wheelchair accessible
Free sensory kits with noise-cancelling headphones, fidgets and sunglasses, plus a Sensory Lounge in Exhibits East
A guest's aide receives complimentary admission
activities.best_time: Monthly 2026-27 series: Dec 30, 2026 and Jan 31, Feb 18, Apr 15 and May 22, 2027 (8-10 a.m.); Mar 27 and Jun 24, 2027 (5-7 p.m.). Confirm on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Request a wheelchair ahead of time if you can, especially for busier visits.
activities.how_to_join: Reserve tickets through the Sensory-Friendly Hours event page or email gs@pacsci.org.

activities.name: Seattle Children's Theatre Access and Sensory-Friendly Performances
activities.price_note: Check current prices on their website; complimentary Personal Care Attendant tickets are available
activities.description: Seattle Children's Theatre's Access performances are sensory-friendly shows that also include ASL interpreting and audio description, and every Mainstage show has a Relaxed or Sensory-Friendly performance plus at least one ASL-interpreted date. It's live theater where every young audience member belongs.
accessibility_notes: Both theatres are accessible to patrons who use wheelchairs or have limited mobility; the accessible entrance is through the Charlotte Martin Theatre lobby on the north side
A hearing loop is installed in both theatres and both Quiet Rooms, with receivers available from the Box Office
Audio description by headphones at Access performances; request Audio Description On Demand at least two weeks ahead
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Ask for seats in the ASL section or near the aisle when you book, and call the Box Office on the day of the show for special accommodations.
activities.how_to_join: Book through sct.org or the Box Office at tickets@sct.org or 206.441.3322 and ask which dates are Access, Sensory-Friendly or ASL performances.

activities.name: Multisensory Storytime at the Washington Talking Book & Braille Library
activities.price_note: No cost is listed; confirm with the library
activities.description: Washington's state library for readers who can't use standard print hosts a storytime for children 0-5 of all abilities: 30 minutes of stories, songs and dance, then 30 minutes of play. Its Children's Room is designed for multisensory exploration, with tactile toys and print/braille board books.
accessibility_notes: Designed for children who are blind or have low vision, with print/braille and large-print board books
Families who can't attend can watch on WTBBL's YouTube channel or request a Storytime Kit mailed home (ages 0-5)
Ask about the accessible entrance and route to the Conference Room before your first visit
activities.best_time: Check today's hours on their website before you go
activities.caregiver_tip: Youth patrons under 18 need a signed Parental Acknowledgment Form on file to use WTBBL services, so send it in early.
activities.venue: Washington Talking Book & Braille Library, 2021 9th Ave
activities.neighborhood: South Lake Union / Denny Triangle, Seattle
activities.how_to_join: Their Youth Services page lists Wednesdays 11 a.m. to noon, but other library pages list Fridays, so call WTBBL at 206-615-0400 to confirm the day.
